_comment: sunbird plugin, run against a LOCAL coverage-instrumented esignet-service.
The mock twin is config.cover.mock.json; read its comment for the server
start-up line, why the address is host.docker.internal, and why
CONFIG_LOCAL=data/config/overlay.none.json is needed.
cd ../api-test && CONFIG_LOCAL=data/config/overlay.none.json \
./run-all.sh -c data/config/config.cover.sunbird.json
sunbird authenticates by knowledge (KBI), so identity.individual_id and
knowledge.{full_name,dob} name a real row in the registry the local server is
pointed at. These are the reference identity already used against the
released registry by the esqa-sunbird deployment profile -- not invented
here, and not this run's own secret, so committed directly the same way
config.mock.json commits its seed identity.
The local server must actually be running the sunbird plugin
(MOSIP_ESIGNET_AUTHN_PROVIDER=sunbird) with
MOSIP_ESIGNET_AUTHENTICATOR_SUNBIRD_RC_AUTH_FACTOR_KBI_REGISTRY_SEARCH_URL
and ..._REGISTRY_GET_URL pointed at https://registry.released.mosip.net/api/v1/Insurance/
(see esignet-service/.env.example) -- these are esignet-service-side settings,
not something the harness itself calls, so api-test carries none of them.
Without them the surfaces report ENV_NOT_READY/failures at runtime and the
coverage panel shows internal/engine/sunbird untouched. The registry is a
public HTTPS endpoint; no VPN/cluster access needed to reach it.
Conformance plans point at the .local.json copies seed-conformance writes --
same clients, same server as the mock cover config, since client-mgmt
registration is plugin-agnostic.
